finding.claim: /transfer accepts a negative amount, so an authenticated user can move money out of any victim account into their own.
finding.source: request.json["amount"] at bank.py:10, attacker-controlled, with no type, sign or range check.

trace.note: amount read from request JSON with no validation
balance check BAL[g.user] < amount is false for negative amount, so abort(400) is skipped

finding.guards_checked: Only guard is the balance check at bank.py:11, which is the wrong direction for negative values. No amount > 0 check, no type validation, no auth check visible in this file. Requires any valid g.user and a known victim account id.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the balance test at bank.py:11 (`BAL[g.user] < amount`), which is false for a negative amount, so abort(400) is skipped. The /withdraw route has an `amount <= 0` check (bank.py:21), but /transfer has no equivalent, and no sign, type or range validation exists anywhere in the directory (bank.py is the only file). Auth for g.user is not defined in this codebase, so the attacker's required role cannot be confirmed from the code. The claim's "authenticated user" framing is therefore unverified, but any caller who can reach /transfer with a valid g.user and an existing victim id can exploit it.

finding.claim: Non-finite amount values (-Infinity, NaN) bypass the balance checks in /transfer and /withdraw, enabling infinite balances or corrupting victim balances to NaN.
finding.source: request.json["amount"] at bank.py:10 (transfer) and bank.py:20 (withdraw). Python json accepts -Infinity and NaN literals by default; relies on Flask's default JSON loader (not executed).
finding.sink: BAL[g.user] -= amount (bank.py:13, bank.py:23) and BAL[to] += amount (bank.py:14).

trace.note: BAL < -inf is false, and BAL < NaN is false, so no abort
-inf amount makes recipient balance -inf; NaN amount makes recipient balance NaN

finding.guards_checked: No math.isfinite or equivalent. Withdraw check amount <= 0 at bank.py:21 does not catch NaN. Same fix as F1 resolves this.

verdict.guard_found: Only the balance comparison at bank.py:11 (`BAL[g.user] < amount`) guards /transfer. With amount=-inf or NaN it evaluates False, so abort(400) is skipped. No isfinite check or input validation exists. Nothing in bank.py sets g.user, so the authentication that sets it is outside this file and I could not check it.
verdict.reason: In /transfer, bank.py:10 takes amount from request.json, and Python's json accepts -Infinity/NaN by default. At bank.py:11 both comparisons are False, so the abort is skipped and bank.py:13-14 set the sender to +inf and the recipient to -inf or NaN, which is confirmed. The candidate's claim that /withdraw with -Infinity bypasses the check is wrong: bank.py:21 `amount <= 0` catches -inf and aborts, so only NaN gets through there, and that only corrupts the caller's own balance.

finding.sink: BAL[to] += amount (bank.py:14) after the non-atomic debit at bank.py:13.

No existence check, transaction, or rollback exists for `to` at bank.py:9-14. `BAL` is a plain dict (bank.py:4), so `BAL[to] += amount` at bank.py:14 raises KeyError after the debit at bank.py:13 has already been applied.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: bank.py:13 debits the sender, then bank.py:14 raises KeyError for an unknown `to`, leaving the debit applied with no guard in between. The only attacker is an authenticated user (g.user is set outside this file, so its origin is unverified), and the loss falls only on that user's own balance (the same loss is available through /withdraw at bank.py:23), so this is a real logic bug with no cross-account security impact.

finding.claim: Check-then-act race on the shared BAL dict lets concurrent withdraws or transfers overdraw an account.
finding.source: Concurrent authenticated requests from the same user to /withdraw (bank.py:20) or /transfer (bank.py:10).
finding.sink: BAL[g.user] -= amount (bank.py:13 and bank.py:23) after a separate read-and-compare at bank.py:11 and bank.py:21.

trace.note: balance check passes for first request
balance check passes for second concurrent withdraw before the first debit lands
both debits applied, balance goes negative

finding.guards_checked: No lock, no conditional UPDATE, no transaction. BAL is a module-level dict shared across threads; Flask threaded mode makes the race reachable. Not executed; plausible under concurrency.

verdict.guard_found: none. No lock, conditional UPDATE, or transaction in bank.py. The only checks are the bare read-and-compare at bank.py:11 and bank.py:21, which run before the unguarded debits at bank.py:13 and bank.py:23. No auth decorator is present, and the directory contains only bank.py.
verdict.reason: The check at bank.py:11 (transfer) and bank.py:21 (withdraw) reads BAL[g.user] and then debits it at bank.py:13 and bank.py:23 with no synchronization, so concurrent requests from one account can both pass the check and overdraw it. The trace lines match the code, though the claim's anchor at bank.py:12 is the abort line rather than the check, and the attacker is an authenticated user only by assumption because g.user is set outside this file. Reachability also depends on the server running threaded, which Flask's dev server does by default.
